sentences.zh: 他写信给他的表弟。

sentences.en: He says, I know the war is terrible and lots of people are dying.
sentences.zh: 他说，我知道战争很残酷，很多人在死去。

sentences.en: He says, but I must say, I shall regret to see the war end.
sentences.zh: 他说，但我必须承认，看不到战争结束我会感到遗憾。

sentences.en: I would be willing, yes, glad to see a battle every day of my life.
sentences.zh: 我愿意，是的，很高兴看到生命中的每一天都在打仗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And there are some people who enjoy wars and who enjoy the thrill, the adrenaline rush.
sentences.zh: 有些人就是喜欢战争，喜欢那种惊险刺激和肾上腺素飙升的感觉。

sentences.en: Custer is one of them.
sentences.zh: 卡斯特就是其中之一。

sentences.en: He does fun things.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢做一些有趣的事。

sentences.en: He goes up in a balloon.
sentences.zh: 他坐热气球升空。

sentences.en: He does go up in a balloon.
sentences.zh: 他确实坐热气球升空了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's a guy who's called Taddeus Lowe, the chief aeronaut of the balloon corps.
sentences.zh: 有个叫塔迪厄斯·洛的人，是气球部队的首席航空员。

sentences.en: And Custer goes up in his craft to look at the Confederate lines and he really likes it.
sentences.zh: 卡斯特坐上了他的飞行器去观察邦联军队的阵地，他真的很喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And then he says, well, I'll go up at night.
sentences.zh: 然后他说，好吧，我要在晚上上去。

sentences.en: You know, unfortunately the Confederates haven't lit enough fires, so he doesn't really get any.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不幸的是，邦联军队没有点燃足够的篝火，所以他实际上什么也没看清。

sentences.en: So he goes up early in the morning, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他一大早就上去了，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he's, he gets up when they're having their breakfaSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他，他趁他们在吃早饭的时候升空。

sentences.en: You know, he does all these things.
sentences.zh: 你看，他做了所有这些事情。

sentences.en: He has locks, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他留着长发，不是吗？

sentences.en: And there is a sort of weird gallantry sometimes to the civil war.
sentences.zh: 内战有时确实有一种奇异的英勇气概。

sentences.en: So there's always moments when there's sort of a pause in the fighting and he'll get invited to kind of Confederate weddings and things.
sentences.zh: 所以总会有那么一些时刻，战斗会出现某种间歇，他会被邀请去参加邦联军官的婚礼之类的事情。

sentences.en: Well, because, you know, lots of his friends from West Point are on the other side.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为，你知道的，他西点军校的许多朋友都在敌对阵营。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And again, there is that sense of a chivalrous rivalry.
sentences.zh: 而且那种骑士般的竞争感依然存在。

sentences.en: So right towards the end of the war, there's this friend of his, a former roommate of his at West Point, Thomas Tex Rosser.
sentences.zh: 所以在战争接近尾声时，有这样一位他的朋友，他西点军校的前室友，托马斯·“特克斯”·罗瑟。

sentences.en: Did you come across him?
sentences.zh: 你遇到过他吗？

sentences.en: I don't know about Tex Rosser.
sentences.zh: 我不了解特克斯·罗瑟。

sentences.en: So they're busy fighting each other and they're trying to capture each other's, you know, kit and wardrobes and things.
sentences.zh: 所以他们忙着互相交战，还试图夺取对方的装备、军服之类东西。

sentences.en: So Tex sends a message to Custer, dear Fanny, I'm sending you a pair of your drawers, which I captured at Trevelyan Street.
sentences.zh: 于是特克斯给卡斯特发了一条消息，亲爱的范妮，我给你寄一条你的衬裤，这是我在特里韦尔安街缴获的。

sentences.en: And Custer replies, asking Tex to direct his tailor to make the coattails a trifle shorter.
sentences.zh: 而卡斯特回复说，请特克斯让他的裁缝把上衣下摆改短一点。

sentences.en: And later he writes to Elizabeth saying that he's captured Tex's raccoon and squirrel from his private menagerie.
sentences.zh: 后来他写信给伊丽莎白，说他从特克斯的私人动物园里缴获了特克斯的浣熊和松鼠。

sentences.en: And they are going hammer and tongs at each other, trying to kill each other.
sentences.zh: 他们打得难分难解，都想置对方于死地。

sentences.en: But at the same time, all kinds of japes involving raccoons and captured clothing.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，又充斥着各种涉及浣熊和缴获衣物的恶作剧。

sentences.en: And that is clearly part of the drama, not just for Custer, but for people on the Confederate side as well.
sentences.zh: 这显然是戏剧性的一部分，不仅对卡斯特如此，对邦联阵营的人来说也是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because of course, that's not the way that all Union officers think of it by any means.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，并非所有联邦军官都是这样看待这场战争的。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 一点也不。

sentences.en: Some are much more sort of grim and dogged and managerial.
sentences.zh: 有些人要冷酷、顽强且富有管理头脑得多。

sentences.en: But Custer is determined to fight this as though it's, you know, a scene from, you know,
sentences.zh: 但卡斯特决心把这场战争打得好像它是一场，你知道的，来自

sentences.en: Mallory or something, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 《亚瑟王之死》之类的场景，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, he really believes in that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他是真的很信仰那一套。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Now, Tom, you mentioned Elizabeth.
sentences.zh: 现在，汤姆，你提到了伊丽莎白。

sentences.en: We haven't introduced her yet.
sentences.zh: 我们还没介绍她呢。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I was jumping the gun.
sentences.zh: 我有点操之过急了。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Custer has caught the eye of the Union commander general, McClellan, and he's joined his staff as his kind of eyes and ears.
sentences.zh: 卡斯特引起了联邦总司令麦克莱恩将军的注意，并作为他的耳目加入了他的参谋部。

sentences.en: Now, he's now hanging around with lots of very impressive people.
sentences.zh: 现在，他开始跟许多了不起的人物混在一起了。

sentences.en: Philippe d'Orléans, is it?
sentences.zh: 是菲利普·德·奥尔良吗？

sentences.en: The pretender to the throne of France is on his staff.
sentences.zh: 法国王位的觊觎者就在他的参谋部里。

sentences.en: So Custer's now moving in a more elevated world.
sentences.zh: 所以卡斯特现在进入了一个更高档的上流社会。

sentences.en: He gets a bit of leave and he goes to Monroe, Michigan, where his sister lives.
sentences.zh: 他获得了一点假期，去了他姐姐居住的密歇根州门罗。

sentences.en: And it's there, isn't it, that he meets Elizabeth Bacon.
sentences.zh: 正是在那里，他遇到了伊丽莎白·培根，不是吗？

sentences.en: Are you a fan of Elizabeth Bacon?
sentences.zh: 你是伊丽莎白·培根的粉丝吗？

sentences.en: He'd met her before, hadn't he?
sentences.zh: 他以前见过她，对吧？

sentences.en: When he was working for the judge as a, you know, a nobody, a kind of young boy.
sentences.zh: 当他给法官打工时，作为一个无名小卒，一个青涩的小伙子。

sentences.en: Supposedly, they have a Thanksgiving party.
sentences.zh: 据说，他们举办了一个感恩节派对。

sentences.en: And this is the real moment when he makes an impression because he's sort of standing there in his uniform and his big hair because he's refusing to cut his hair.
sentences.zh: 这才是他真正留下深刻印象的时刻，因为他穿着制服站在那里，留着一头长发，因为他拒绝剪头发。

sentences.en: He says, I won't cut my hair until we capture Richmond, Virginia, the sort of Confederate capital.
sentences.zh: 他说，在攻克弗吉尼亚州的里士满——那个邦联的首都之前，我是不会剪头发的。

sentences.en: And he looks very gallant at this party and he captures Elizabeth's attention.
sentences.zh: 他在这个派对上看起来英姿飒爽，一下子吸引了伊丽莎白的注意。

sentences.en: She is sort of small.
sentences.zh: 她个子有点矮。

sentences.en: She's brown haired.
sentences.zh: 她留着棕色的头发。

sentences.en: She's pretty, but she's very serious, isn't she, Elizabeth?
sentences.zh: 她很漂亮，但又非常严肃，对吧，伊丽莎白？

sentences.en: Are you an Elizabeth fan?
sentences.zh: 你是伊丽莎白的粉丝吗？

sentences.en: Libby?
sentences.zh: 莉比？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm absolutely an Elizabeth fan.
sentences.zh: 对，我绝对是伊丽莎白的粉丝。

sentences.en: I mean, spoiler alert, she adores Custer.
sentences.zh: 我是说，剧透一下，她对卡斯特崇拜得五体投地。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And burnishes his legend very, very effectively.
sentences.zh: 而且非常非常有效地擦拭和装点着他的传奇。

sentences.en: She does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: You know, and I like to see a successful marriage.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我乐见美满的婚姻。

sentences.en: But the judge doesn't approve is not a Custer.
sentences.zh: 但法官并不赞同，觉得他不是个理想的卡斯特人选。

sentences.en: He describes him as that moustached fellow.
sentences.zh: 他形容卡斯特是“那个留着八字胡的家伙”。

sentences.en: And he says, he's already slept with three girls from the town.
sentences.zh: 并且他说，他已经跟镇上的三个女孩睡过觉了。

sentences.en: What do you want to have anything to do with him for?
sentences.zh: 你为什么还要跟他扯上关系？

sentences.en: I mean, he, again, if you think of, we talked about Custer's father looking absolutely like you would expect a mid to 19th century American Methodist to look like.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他——同样地，如果你回想一下，我们说过卡斯特的父亲看起来完全就像你期望的那种19世纪中期的美国卫理公会教徒。

sentences.en: If you imagine an intimidating judge from the same period, he's kind of very bald, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 如果你想象一个同一时期的令人生畏的法官，他基本上是个秃头，对吧？

sentences.en: Very kind of rock solid, very much not the kind of man who would enjoy a man who's allowing his hair to grow out.
sentences.zh: 非常坚定顽固，绝不是那种会欣赏一个任由头发生长的人的类型。

sentences.en: Or japes.
sentences.zh: 或者说喜欢恶作剧的人。

sentences.en: Or japes.
sentences.zh: 或者说喜欢恶作剧。

sentences.en: And pranks.
sentences.zh: 和胡闹。

sentences.en: Yeah, he wouldn't be a fan of that whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 对，他绝对不会喜欢这一套。

sentences.en: He would not be a fan of that, especially not with his beloved daughter.
sentences.zh: 他绝不会喜欢那样的人，尤其是对方打起他宝贝女儿的主意时。

sentences.en: No, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，一点也不。

sentences.en: So actually, they say no.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，他们拒绝了。

sentences.en: Custer is rebuffed.
sentences.zh: 卡斯特吃了闭门羹。

sentences.en: He's basically sent back, you know, see if you can make something of yourself.
sentences.zh: 他基本上被轰了回去，你知道的，先去证明自己能干出点名堂再说。

sentences.en: And actually, he does make something of himself because he goes back to the front.
sentences.zh: 而事实上，他也确实干出了名堂，因为他回到了前线。

sentences.en: And in the summer of 1863, he is promoted at the age of 23 to Brigadier General.
sentences.zh: 在1863年夏天，23岁的他被晋升为准将。

sentences.en: And it's at that point that he really goes to town on designing his own outfit.
sentences.zh: 正是在那个时候，他开始极其高调地设计自己的战袍。

sentences.en: I love this, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个了，汤姆。

sentences.en: I love somebody who designs his own costume.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢自己设计服装的人。

sentences.en: I love it too.
sentences.zh: 我也很喜欢。

sentences.en: It's very Nelsonian, I think, this, or Napoleonic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很有纳尔逊或拿破仑的风范。

sentences.en: So he has his big hat, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他有一顶大帽子，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a Confederate hat.
sentences.zh: 这是一顶邦联军帽。

sentences.en: Yeah, which he always wears sort of on one side, like a felt hat.
sentences.zh: 对，他总是把它戴得稍微偏向一侧，就像一顶呢帽。

sentences.en: Well, because he says that he has very fair skin.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为他说自己的皮肤非常白。

sentences.en: So he's worried about that.
sentences.zh: 所以他对此很担心。

sentences.en: But as you say, he wears it at a jaunty angle.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，他戴得很有俏皮的斜角。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And you've mentioned how he's growing his hair.
sentences.zh: 而且你提过他是怎么留头发的。

sentences.en: And he says he won't cut it until he's, you know, the Union have taken Richmond.
sentences.zh: 他说在北方联邦攻克里士满之前，你知道的，他绝不剪头发。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And of course, this is pure vanity.
sentences.zh: 当然，这完全是出于虚荣。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全是。

sentences.en: But also quite odd because his nickname is still Fanny.
sentences.zh: 但同时也挺奇怪的，因为他的绰号依然叫“范妮”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: You know, he's got a girl's hairstyle.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他留着个女孩子的发型。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But he's setting it off with this sensational military uniform.
sentences.zh: 但他用这身极其抢眼的军服来衬托它。

sentences.en: Well, he's got this black velvet jacket.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他穿着这件黑色天鹅绒夹克。

sentences.en: It's a Hussar's jacket, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一件轻骑兵夹克，对吧？

sentences.en: Embroidered with gold.
sentences.zh: 上面绣着金线。

sentences.en: Lots of gold on it.
sentences.zh: 上面有大量的金饰。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Gold piping.
sentences.zh: 金色饰边。

sentences.en: And underneath the black sort of velvet Hussar's jacket, he wears a sailor's shirt with stars sewn into it.
sentences.zh: 在这件黑色的轻骑兵天鹅绒夹克里面，他还穿着一件缝着星星的水手衫。

sentences.en: I think stars sewn into your sailor's shirt is an unusual look.
sentences.zh: 我觉得水手衫上缝星星是一种很不寻常的造型。

sentences.en: And a huge red cravat.
sentences.zh: 还有一条巨大的红色领结。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And massive boots and spurs and all that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 以及巨大的靴子、马刺之类的一切。

sentences.en: He's got gold lace on his pants.
sentences.zh: 他的裤子上还有金色的饰带。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: All of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的一切。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the thing is, there is a sort of sense to this.
sentences.zh: 关键是，这样做其实是有一定道理的。

sentences.en: Because if you're the kind of commander that Custer is, i.e.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你是卡斯特那种类型的指挥官，也就是说——

sentences.en: Someone who leads from the front, not somebody who's planning at the back, but somebody who is absolutely leading your men into action, as let's say Nelson did,
sentences.zh: 那种冲在最前面而不是在后方运筹帷幄的指挥官，那种真正带领手下投入战斗的人，就像我们说的纳尔逊那样，

sentences.en: you want to stand out.
sentences.zh: 你会希望自己格外显眼。

sentences.en: Now, people who listen to the Trafalgar episodes will remember that Nelson refused to change his coat at Trafalgar because he said, my men need to see me.
sentences.zh: 听过特拉法加海战那几期节目的听众会记得，纳尔逊当年在特拉法加拒绝换下外套，因为他说，我的部下需要看到我。

sentences.en: They need to see the commander.
sentences.zh: 他们需要看到指挥官。

sentences.en: And Custer, I think, operates with the same.
sentences.zh: 我认为卡斯特也是按同样的逻辑行事的。

sentences.en: He is the star.
sentences.zh: 他就是那颗星。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He is the hero of the story.
sentences.zh: 他就是这个故事里的英雄。

sentences.en: Everybody needs to look at him.
sentences.zh: 所有人都需要看着他。

sentences.en: I mean, you can absolutely make the military case for it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你完全可以从军事角度为他辩护。

sentences.en: And Custer does make the military case for it.
sentences.zh: 卡斯特也确实为自己这样做进行过军事上的辩解。

sentences.en: The difference between him and Nelson.
sentences.zh: 但他和纳尔逊的区别在于：

sentences.en: Nelson is entitled to wear those medals.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊有资格佩戴那些勋章。

sentences.en: You know, he is an officer in the Navy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是海军军官。

sentences.en: Custer is going absolutely freelance, as he always does throughout his entire career, and making up a costume.
sentences.zh: 而卡斯特完全是独断专行，就像他整个职业生涯中一贯的那样，自己设计了一套戏服。

sentences.en: And I do think that that, the long hair, everything.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为，长发以及这一切……

sentences.en: Sure, it's about enabling people on the battlefield to see him.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是为了让战场上的人能看到他。

sentences.en: But clearly, it's all.
sentences.zh: 但很显然，这一切……

sentences.en: I mean, he's.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他……

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，完全是。

sentences.en: Sensationally vain.
sentences.zh: 极度虚荣。

sentences.en: He's very vain.
sentences.zh: 他非常虚荣。

sentences.en: He's very vain.
sentences.zh: 他非常虚荣。

sentences.en: But he's good.
sentences.zh: 但他确实很优秀。

sentences.en: I don't think we should lose sight of that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们不应该忽视这一点。

sentences.en: And I think in his biography, TJ Stiles says, one of the problems with writing about Custer or telling his story is that everyone starts with his death.
sentences.zh: 我想TJ·斯泰尔斯在他的传记中说过，撰写卡斯特的生平或讲述他的故事时，遇到的一个问题是大家都从他的死开始说起。

sentences.en: We started with his death.
sentences.zh: 我们是从他的死开始讲起的。

sentences.en: You know, we started with the Harry Flashman.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们是从《哈利·弗莱士曼》式的视角开始的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So we start with the presumption of incompetence and failure or hubris and arrogance.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一开始就带着无能、失败、狂妄或傲慢的预设。

sentences.en: But actually, the point about Custer in the Civil War, he's good.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，关于卡斯特在内战中的表现，他很优秀。

sentences.en: He makes good decisions.
sentences.zh: 他能做出正确的决策。

sentences.en: He inspires his men.
sentences.zh: 他能激励他的部下。

sentences.en: I mean, armies need stars.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，军队需要明星。

sentences.en: And he is a star.
sentences.zh: 而他就是一颗星。

sentences.en: And he doesn't make bad calls.
sentences.zh: 他没有做出过糟糕的决策。
